metadata.note: Sandusky, MI (Sanilac County, in Michigan's 'Thumb') did have passenger rail -- but research turned up a correction worth flagging: the two lines that actually served it were NOT Grand Trunk Western. By 1900 Sandusky was served by (1) the Pere Marquette Railroad's Sanilac Railroad branch, built west from Carsonville/Poland to Sandusky and completed June 1903, and (2) the Detroit, Bay City and Western Railroad (DBC&W), an independently-built line (not GTW, though it crossed Michigan Central spur tracks at Bay City) constructed 1907-1916 running Bay City-Caro-Sandusky-Peck-Port Huron -- one of the last new railroads built in Michigan, running up to three daily round trips in 1916. DBC&W went bankrupt in 1925 and was reorganized as the Detroit, Caro and Sandusky Railway (DC&S). The Bay City-Caro segment lost passenger service to automobile competition and was scrapped in 1928 after flood damage; the line was progressively cut back from both ends (Fargo-Roseburg, then Roseburg-Peck) until Sandusky became the railway's final terminal in 1948; the very last run, Caro-Sandusky, was June 8 1953. Grand Trunk Western did have its own Detroit-Port Huron secondary main with branches to Saginaw and Bay City, but those ran a different, more southerly routing and did not pass through Sandusky itself. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation, straight-line segments between documented stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps.

https://www.michiganrailroads.com/stories/5280-history-of-the-detroit-caro-and-sandusky-railway (Bay City-Caro segment scrapped 1928 after flood damage, auto competition had already ended its passenger service; progressive abandonment Fargo-Roseburg then Roseburg-Peck; Sandusky became the line's final terminal 1948; last run to Sandusky June 8 1953)

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
